newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins slip after strong rise, seen up.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins slip after strong rise, seen up.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds weakened on Thursday in quiet trading as the market paused for breath after strong gains on Wednesday, dealers said.
"Everyone is sleeping after yesterday's battle," an International Moscow Bank dealer said. "Everything is a bit softer and it looks like it will go on like this until the end of the day."
A Western banker in Moscow forecast a slight price rise in the next few days.
"If prices fall people will use it as a chance to buy cheaply," he said. "The market should go up next week."
But the International Moscow Bank dealer said the market would be quiet in the next few days waiting for next Thursday's U.S. payrolls figures.
"Trading will be range-bound for the next few day until Thursday, when U.S. economic figures come out," he said.

He said the market was expecting an inflow of fresh funds from the Treasury bill market over the longer term after First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov's promise on Thursday that the government would continue to push interest rates down.
The dealer said that the funds would start flowing in when the yield on GKO discount Treasury bills fell to 13-14 percent from the current 18-19 percent.
The market is waiting for the Finance Ministry to start publishing the volume of fully reconciled debt to the London Club of commercial bank creditors, he said.
The larger the amount reconciled, the more investors will be positive towards Russian debt and prepared to buy MinFins, he said.
A senior Finance Ministry official promised the ministry would start publishing reconciliations from August on a weekly basis.
